entities.name: Publius Aelius Paetus
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Publius Aelius Paetus was a Roman consul of the late 3rd century BC, serving under Scipio Africanus. He was born into a prominent equestrian family and rose to prominence through his military service.

 Paetus played a key role in Africanus's campaigns against Carthage, distinguishing himself at the Battle of Zama in 202 BC. After Africanus's death in 146 BC, Paetus was elected censor with Africanus's adopted son, Scipio Aemilianus. As censor, he oversaw significant reforms to Rome's government and administration.

 Despite his significant contributions to Roman history, Paetus's life remains somewhat of a mystery due to the scarcity of historical records from this period. His legacy as a loyal supporter of Africanus and a skilled military leader continues to fascinate historians today.

 The fact that Paetus was elected censor with Scipio Aemilianus underscores the significant influence he had on Roman politics during this time, particularly in shaping the city's governance and institutions.
